body:
Flat out, this is going to be the @#$%tiest TR I will ever do (even if it is a double).  I can’t even remember the witty, attention catching phrase that came up on the ride home for a title.  I’m tired and have a headache but I need to document my games so I’m posting brief details of them, and even briefer (is that a word?) details about the time surrounding them.  To attempt to make up for that I will post the decks I used (as best I can remember).  I am also going to copy and pasting this to Note Pad, then copy and pasting it to Decktech (instead of editing out all the punctuation then manually adding it all back in) so sorry if the tabs show up.



9/6:  Thursday.  School.  Drive up to Phoenix with Enrique Huerta.  Spend the night at Girard’s place in the middle of nowhere.  He has funny dogs.



9/7:  Friday.  DPC day and only 25 show up for it.  Gay.   Rating is 2261.  Decks are WYS SOLID and HDADTJ SOLID.

Hunt Down And Destroy The Jedi/Their Fire Has Gone Out Of The Universe



Game One

WYS Vs Chris Schaut’s (1865) Senate

WYS doesn’t lose to senate, as far as I’m aware.

FW +29

2(+29)



Highs:  Seeing Chris again.  He’s from New York.

Lows:  Me no know.



Game Two

HDADTJ Vs John Hawkins’ (2070) WYS

I got excellent draw.  I got lots of force, and applied much pressure forcing him to delay flipping.  Vader + Cantina + Stick = drain.  2x ZIMH + 2x Lat Damage = beats.

FW +17

4(+46)



Highs:  Playing John.  He is an excellent player.

Lows:  None.



Game Three

WYS Vs Tim Guzman’s (1935) HDADTJ

The game was actually pretty even because he got a pretty good start, in comparison to mine.  Eventually Vader went Lost in the Wilderness, and that basically sealed it.  Edges help differential.

FW +23

6(+69!)



Highs:  Tim is the man.  He smells like a doctor.

Lows:  This @#$%ing headache.



Game Four

HDADTJ Vs Chris Denoma’s (2030) WYS

Much like John’s except no racing.  Fitting that I beat him by 6 more cards.  Vader just likes to drain.

FW +23

8(+22)



Highs:  Chris is a really cool guy.  Check out his and John’s site www.CCGHookup.com

Lows:  Philosophy papers I should be writing.



Game Five

WYS Vs Clint Hays’ (2226) Senate

He never got the combo, and Vader found his @#$% beaten by swarming smugglers.  Lost in the Wilderness mighta been played, and Dodge was a pain in his ass.

FW +22

10(+114)



Highs:  Playing (and beating) Clint for the first time.

Lows:  None, it was a good game all around.



Game Six

HDADTJ Vs Clint Hays’ (Julien Riviere’s) (2226) MYWHL

You’ve seen the deck lists.  This deck was designed to rape mains and toys and that’s exactly what it did to me.  That, coupled with the fact that I didn’t flip for 6 turns because I couldn’t draw a Vader, or I couldn’t get a battleground for him to go to means an easy win for him.  I drew up when Clint had 10 cards on his racer, 12 in his hand, and 6+ cards in his lost pile.

FL -23

10(+91)



Highs:  It only took about 7 minutes to play.

Lows:  AFA should only work if they occupy a battleground.



I finish in first.  Josh Bader from Colorado got second.  Then Chu was one differential ahead of Clint for third.  Chu beats Josh by one card, cause he’s that damned good, and I play Clint.



Semi Finals

WYS Vs Clint’s Senate

Same as before.  Vader got his @#$% smacked, and I just controlled the board (Menace Fades, Battle Plan, Goo Nee Tay, etc).  I didn’t care about differential, so I just played to win.

FW +17



The prize money was weak and Chu and I discovered that even if he won first he and Clint weren’t going to break even (plane tickets, hotel etc).  We both knew that our light decks would win, but his light would have won by more (probably) so rather than forcing him to risk losing any more money I agreed to give him the first place cash.



That night we all just kinda hung out.  I got Juz into L5R.  Helped Jay Webb Build decks for the open.



9/8:  Saturday.  I had to get my lazy @#$% out of bed at 8:00 to run the open.  After 6 it was John Hawkins in first and Chu in second.  Chu won both games of the final.  I played in a Raw Deal tourney and sucked cause the deck I borrowed was ass.  Went to Hooters with Juz, Clint, and Jay Webb.



[Scene Missing]



[Scene Missing]



Went to bed at 4am.



9/9:  Sunday.  Up at 12 to run tourney at 1.  No one comes.  Screw around for a bit.  Go to lunch with Juz and Enrique.  Play L5R.  Go home.



Epilogue (sort of)



9/11:  Terrorist attacks.



10/3:  DecipherCon is cancelled.



10/5:  I quit SW.



10/7:  I return.



10/10:  Wednesday.  A monthly tournament at the Gamer’s Edge in Phoenix.  Haven’t played since DPC Phoenix.  Been busy juggling Katie and Allie, so I build my dark in the car on the drive up with Enrique, Justin Beal, Bobby Dayton, and Pat Gimber.  I get to ride in the trunk of the Blazer.  Suck.  Bobby has to piss like a racehorse since he drank like 1.5 liters of Dr. Pepper before we left.  Much laughter ensues as we declare that pit stops are determined not by the one with weakest bladder, but by the one with the strongest, as dictated by the code of man.  Rating is 2278.  Decks are WYS SOLID and Martin Falke’s second version of his Senate, both with slight modifications.



Game One

Falke Senate Vs Jon Dunn’s (1785) HB Operatives

Lots of senators, lots of squabbles and yet I don’t flip for 230597823048 turns.  Literally.  Third turn I get Maul in his ship to Kirdo III, which is good.  I beat up EPP Luke with Palp (who he failed to kill), Dr. E & Ponda, IG with Gun and an I Have You Now for eight, I think.  Then Thrawn + Chimaera + Lat damage on lone Wedge in ship seals it.

FW + 19



Highs:  I like John.  He silly.  Deck fun.

Lows:  Kinda non-interactive.



Game Two

WYS Vs Robert Dayton’s (1644) Maul Hut/ JP Start

Bobby is seriously one of the best players I have encountered out here.  If he was more competitive I’m sure he could easily be rated at least 2000.  We’ve played this match up a couple times in testing, so we knew each other’s decks to a t (what does is that supposed to mean, anyway?) and we both knew I was going to win.  To be a great sport, he drew up to give me the full win.  Mad Props for that, bud.

FW + 22



Highs:  Its cool playing Bobby.

Lows:  Playing one another hurt our "team" from Tucson.



Game Three

Falke Senate Vs Robert Dayton’s (1644) TIGIH

Again, I know his deck inside and out and I know how to beat it, but I play like a complete @#$% wipe.  DTF/ First Strike did more damage to me than anything all game.  Eventually Vader took Luke and hid on the Executor DB, and ZiMH drained at Kashyyyk for the win.

FW+ 7



Highs:  Bleh.

Lows:  I suck at this game.



Game Four

WYS Vs Justin Beal’s (1751) Droid AOBS

I can satisfy Battle Plan and he can’t.  I am activating more than he is.  We skirmish, but I always come out on top.  We waste a lot of time trying to figure out how much he can lose by and still come in second as I play with my Edges, and time is called and I find myself with the timed win.  My 21 cards to his 2.

TW + 21



Highs:  None.

Lows:  I’m stupid.  I lose points now.



I win, Beal grabs second, Enrique ran the thing, but would have gotten third, and Bobby and Pat scrub out hardcore.  We attempt to eat at Jack in the Box, but they are out of shakes so I opt for nothing.  After 5 minutes of watching them eat I want food and settle for spicy Doritos and a coffee coollatta thing from 7-11.  Many odd things are said on the way home, the end result of which being that Bobby is a flaming homo.



Mad Props to:



Bobby for being a great sport and an excellent playtest buddy.



Props to:



Kiki cause he’s always driving and running tournaments, unselfishly.



See you all at "A World Champioship" in Virginia Beach this November.  I forget if there is anything else I have to say.  Good night.



-Hayes "Hayes" Hunter

summary: Hayes Hunter finished the Swiss of the 25-player 2001 Phoenix DPC in first place with Watch Your Step and Hunt Down And Destroy The Jedi, going 5–1 (10 (+91)), and beat Clint Hays in the semifinal; he then gave Jonny Chu the first-place prize money instead of playing out the final. The report also covers the next day's Phoenix Open, which he ran, and a 10 October 2001 Gamer's Edge tournament that he won 4–0.
notes: No hub for a September 2001 Phoenix DPC on the List or live; named '2001 Phoenix DPC' (caller's instruction), with the Saturday open as '2001 Phoenix Open' (parent the DPC). Dates from the report (9/7 Friday DPC, 9/8 Saturday open). Site given only as Phoenix.
Format Premiere - Coruscant: September 2001 DPC with Senate decks; the List gives the 2001 Denver DPC (1 September) as Premiere - Coruscant.

Winner left null: after the semifinals (Hunter beat Hays; Chu beat Josh Bader 'by one card') Hunter 'agreed to give him [Chu] the first place cash' rather than make Chu risk losing more money; the report does not say whether the final was played or who was recorded as champion. Hunter's finish recorded as '1st after Swiss'.
Swiss standings stated: Hunter 1st, Josh Bader (from Colorado) 2nd, Chu 3rd 'one differential ahead of Clint', Hays 4th.
Record 6–1 = 5–1 Swiss plus the semifinal win. Points 10 (+91) from the last Swiss line; margins sum to +91. The printed '8(+22)' after game 4 is a typo for +92.
Clint Hays faced three times (rounds 5 and 6 and the semifinal), as the report says; in round 6 he played Julien Riviere's MYWHL deck (read as Mind What You Have Learned).
Full decklists for both decks are included in the report.
Small-world mappings: John Hawkins, Chris Denoma (both of CCGHookup.com), Tim Guzman, Chris Schaut, Clint Hays, Josh Bader and Jonny Chu ('Chu') to their existing pages.
Sunday 9 September: Hunter was to run a tournament at 1 pm but 'No one comes'; no event.

Second side event: the 10 October 2001 monthly tournament at the Gamer's Edge in Phoenix (also covered by Robert Dayton's reports d3051 and d3056), named 'October 2001 Phoenix tournament'. Enrique Huerta ran it ('would have gotten third' is hypothetical, not recorded).
Oct 10 game 1 opponent 'Jon Dunn' (later 'I like John') mapped to the existing Jon Dunn page (Phoenix-area Hexacon player).
Oct 10 scores differ from Robert Dayton's report d3051: Hunter gives FW +22 and FW +7 against Dayton; Dayton gives losses of 7 and 24. See discrepancies.
The remark about Bobby Dayton is kept verbatim (Bill 2026-10-25: no content holds). Title is not crude.
